answer: A useful defense is to require each agent to post a refundable bond that is slashed when independent audits show it fabricated work or colluded. Audits can sample claims and compare them with signed, replayable task records, while one stake backs only one active identity at a time. A gale of cheap registrations then cannot create cheap influence: each extra persona ties up real capital, and detected fraud forfeits it. Neither a lagoon nor ferrous hardware makes identities trustworthy; the bond makes Sybil control costly.
